playoff.note: single-leg knock-out at the higher seed; the winner takes the third promotion place (top two go up automatically)
single-leg knock-out; the winner takes the second promotion place if it holds a J2 licence

boundaries.note: J2: top two automatic, 3rd-6th play off for the third place. J1: bottom three relegated, no J1/J2 play-off since 2024.
J3: top two automatic, 3rd-6th play off for the third place (J2 licence required). J2: bottom three relegated.

JFL champion replaces J3's 20th automatically if it holds a J3 licence; JFL runner-up plays the J3 19th-placed club if it holds one. If neither JFL club is licensed, nothing moves and J3 relegates nobody (so 0-2 down).

notes: 2026-27 is the FIRST autumn-spring season in J.League history: J1 runs 7 Aug 2026 - 6 Jun 2027, J2/J3 from 8 Aug, JFL 29 Aug 2026 - 23 May 2027. Membership of 2026-27 was decided by the 2025 calendar-year season (3 relegated from J1, 3 promoted from J2), not by the 2026 half-season. The first half of 2026 was filled by the one-off J1 100 Year Vision League (6 Feb - 7 Jun 2026): the same 20 J1 clubs split into East/West groups of ten, double round-robin, penalty shoot-outs for draws (2 pts win / 1 pt loss), then a prize playoff - explicitly no relegation and no bearing on 2026-27 places. So Japan played three competitions in 2026: 2025 J1 (calendar year, finished Dec 2025), the 100 Year Vision League (Feb-Jun 2026), and 2026-27 (from Aug 2026). The JFL followed the J.League: 2025 was its last calendar-year season, 2026-27 its first autumn-spring one. All four divisions are single tables, double round-robin (20 clubs = 38 rounds, 16 clubs = 30). J1 has been 20 clubs since 2024, when the 3-down-without-play-off rule also started. JFL now relegates its bottom two (15th and 16th) directly to the regional leagues, replacing the old 15th-place play-off, so JFL closed_down is true in our data and its bottom two really do leave.
